hypothesis: With feedback bounded throughout warmup, continuing local feedback adaptation reduces post-change loss versus freezing without excessive loss of old knowledge.
task: Synthetic context-indexed binary relations; old contexts 0-3, novel contexts 4-5, drift reverses relations 0/1 in context 0.

model.representation: complete orthonormal real Fourier coefficients, dense rule then full encode, no truncation

warmup.feedback: bounded and unbounded shadow paths; no exact hidden gradients supplied

online.schedule: identical predetermined data schedule across arms

bound.method: multiply each B/V/U matrix and its coefficients by min(1, 2*(1-4*machine_epsilon)/sigma_max) at each applicable step; full SVD values

primary.metric: mean of 16 checkpoint cross-entropies; relative reduction within seed, then mean across seeds
primary.effect_gate: mean relative reduction >=5% and no negative seed
primary.retention_guard: old accuracy loss <=2 percentage points during primary window and at final, in every seed

failure_policy: stop affected arm, retain state and failed prefix; continue controls; no retuning
scope: SAM-inspired synthetic diagnostic; no language-model, novelty, efficiency or exact-paper-replication claim.
